Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PSIC-01 Psicologia generale, neuropsicologia e neuroscienze cognitive, psicometria

The candidate will be involved in ongoing research related to the project. Besides assisting the group in MEG data collection and preprocessing, the candidate will conduct their own research project to investigate whether predictive neural representations of body posture and position of an observed ice skater can be separated into a ventral 'what' and dorsal 'where' prediction stream, respectively. Last, the candidate will be involved in the methodological development of the dynamic RSA method, which is the methodological backbone of the entire project.

The research activity will investigate effective visualization strategies for representing and communicating complex data, using 'à contrainte' literature as a case study. By analysing formal constraints and combinatorial practices, different data visualization models and modes of interaction will be tested. The research will assess how effectively these visual solutions make complex information structures accessible, explorable, and understandable to different types of users to guarantee scalability and reuse.

item.title: Incarico di ricerca: Electrophysiological investigation of social interactions in premotor and limbic brain regions (cingulate cortex and amygdala) in non-human primates. (Univ. PARMA)
item.description:
Deadline: 2026-10-31 23:59
Institution: Univ. PARMA, Parma
Field: History, philosophy, education, psychology / 11/PSIC-01 Psicologia generale, neuropsicologia e neuroscienze cognitive, psicometria

The research program within which this position is embedded investigates how the brain encodes and generates social and emotional behaviors by examining the underlying neuronal mechanisms and neural circuits. The research requires the use of macaques housed in dedicated animal facilities, as only non-human primates with a brain organization closely resembling that of humans allow the development and validation of these methodologies. The overall goal is to advance our understanding of the neural processes underlying social and emotional interactions, with potential implications for improving the understanding and treatment of psychiatric and neurological disorders.
